evidence.t: GLD fell 0.5% vs a typical daily move of 1.6% (last 60 days), so no classification is triggered. Over 5 days it fell 3.1%.
The Fed raised rates for the first time since 2023; the 10-year real rate rose 0.47 points over the month to 29 Sep.

past.reaction: Not measured: gold reacts to rates and the dollar far more than to this report.
take: Buying has shifted from consumers to central banks: jewellery tonnes -17% while central banks +62%, each vs Q2 2025.
Central banks: Q2 was a record second quarter, but the first half (345 t) was the lowest since 2022, after WGC cut Q1 to 57 t (from 244 t).
Jewellery spending in dollars still rose (first half +22% vs a year earlier, $86bn, WGC press release): fewer tonnes at a much higher price.
Gold ETFs worldwide saw a 44.8 t outflow in Q2 (first half +18 t).
past.impact: Feeds DM4 (central banks, last 4 quarters -20.5% vs the 4 before: bearish, mostly from the Q1 reclassification) and DM5 (jewellery plus bars and coins -10.1% vs Q2 2025: bearish).

calendar.t: World Gold Council Gold Demand Trends Q3 (expected)
calendar.note: Estimated: about end-October (Q2 came out Thu 30 Jul). Updates DM4 central banks and DM5 consumer demand.

lead: GLD's reading is building history (today's zone: Sell, −40 on a −100 to +100 scale, down from −34 on 1 Oct): rising real interest rates and a firmer dollar are pressing on gold, and today's slide came from selling pressure: shares traded on down days outweighed up days by about 1.45 to 1 over the last 20 trading days. Read it as a pressure gauge, not a timing signal.
bullets: Rates are the main pressure. The 10-year real interest rate is 2.88% on 1 Oct vs 2.45% on 2 Sep (+0.43 points, bearish); the dollar index rose 2.92 points over 20 trading days (bearish). Net Fed odds (chance of a cut minus chance of a rise) moved 5.9 points towards cuts in 28 days, under the 15-point line (neutral).

Liquidity weakened to −53 from −13. Selling volume dominates: shares traded on down days were about 1.45 times those on up days over the last 20 trading days (the up-day vs down-day volume ratio is 0.69x, bearish; it was neutral on 1 Oct). GLD's own gold holdings were 1,056.55 t on 1 Oct, unchanged within 0.1% from 20 sessions earlier (neutral), and hedge funds' net long position in gold futures is at the 52nd percentile of the last 3 years (neutral).

The price trend is down. $380.14 is 8.7% below its 200-day average and the 50-day average is 4.8% below the 200-day (both bearish); over 3 months GLD is 3.2 points behind the S&P 500 (neutral). Price trend bucket −72 on −100 to +100.

Demand is mixed, and one figure tips it to Sell. Central bank buying is 20.5% lower over 4 quarters vs the 4 before (780 t vs 981 t, bearish), mostly because WGC moved 187 t of Q1 2026 into another category, so it counts at half weight (6 of 12 points) until WGC's Q3 report; on WGC's first Q1 figure it would be neutral and the composite about −32 (still Sell, below the −30 line). Consumer buying is 10.1% lower vs a year earlier (bearish); GLD's gold holdings rose 5.4% in 60 trading days (bullish). Demand bucket −41.
Not stretched to an extreme. GLD is 38.5% above its 200-week average (bearish only at 60%+) and gold vs the S&P 500 is 13.5% above its 10-year median (bearish at 25%+). Valuation (stretch) bucket 0.

Not a call yet. Day 3 of 10. Confidence High means only that data coverage is 100% and 3 of 4 buckets agree, not that the reading has a good record: in the 5-year replay, weeks reading Sell were followed by GLD +12.9% over 6 months on average (vs +10.8% for all weeks).
defects: Staging build, first day: a call needs 7 of the last 10 trading days in one zone.
The day's move breakdown keeps the stock wording: 'Sector' = SPY's move beyond the S&P 500 (near zero), 'Company-specific' = gold's own move.

Today's zone turns on one figure: central bank buying (DM4) reads -20.5% mostly because WGC moved 187 t of Q1 2026 into another category. It counts at half weight (6 of 12 points, Kenneth 1 Oct) until WGC's Q3 2026 report (~29 Oct). On WGC's first Q1 figure DM4 is neutral and the composite about -32 (still Sell).
10-year real rate (G-DM1) is published by FRED a day late: latest value 29 Sep.

Stretch (G-VL1): the 200-week average counts the current week twice (Yahoo repeats it): $274.48 instead of $273.42, so +38.7% instead of +39.3%. The score is unaffected (bearish only at 60%+); engine fix pending.
Fed odds (LQ6) use the shared engine's 28-day window and are jumpy: rise odds were 48% on 29 Sep and 34% on 30 Sep; on 29 Sep LQ6 would have read bearish (composite about -36).
GLD flows (G-LQ2, G-DM3) cover GLD only, not all gold funds worldwide.
Hedge-fund positioning (G-LQ3) is weekly: latest report as of Tue 22 Sep, released Fri 25 Sep.
Sensitivity to the S&P 500 (0.80x, last 252 trading days) is computed from daily GLD and index moves; gold has been unusually correlated with stocks in 2026.

5-year weekly replay (research/sanity_check.md): Sell readings in 2021-26 were followed by GLD +12.9% over 6 months on average vs +10.8% for all weeks; stretch at extremes was the best input, real rates the weakest.
